paragraphs.text: Routine records describe vision after laser capsulotomy, but the availability and methods of measurement vary. A summary of recorded change must preserve missingness and distinguish unique people from treated eyes; these observations cannot establish a laser treatment effect.

The primary objective is to describe fixed-study-eye distance visual-acuity change from the historical baseline to the Day 42 selection window. The secondary objective is to describe recorded early pressure elevation in that eye. This review is descriptive; no comparative treatment hypothesis or exploratory endpoint is proposed.

Include all eligible consecutive ordinary-care records at Elmstead Ophthalmology Clinic, anticipating 150 unique adults aged 50–90 at their first eligible procedure. All sexes are eligible; healthy volunteers are not included. One fixed eye contributes outcomes per person. Repeated records or procedures do not create additional people.

Exclude the person only if no eligible eye remains. Select one study eye: earliest eligible laser, right eye if both on the same date. Deduplicate patients; never switch eyes for missing data. Missing measurements affect only the relevant analysis, not cohort eligibility. Other eye disease is recorded context, not an automatic exclusion. No screening washout or other-study restriction. Pregnancy status is not collected and creates no restriction; no children.

lists.label: Inclusion criteria
items: Age 50 through 90 inclusive at the first eligible procedure.
Routine laser capsulotomy at Elmstead Ophthalmology Clinic from 1 January through 31 August 2025 inclusive.
Reliably identifiable person, procedure date and treated eye.
Records accessible under required ethics/privacy decisions and site permission.

lists.label: Exclusion criteria applied to eyes
items: An eye whose laser was part of an interventional research protocol.
An eye whose identity or procedure date cannot be verified.

paragraphs.text: This single-site retrospective observational cohort reviews routine laser capsulotomy for clinician-documented posterior capsule opacification. Treatment and subsequent care were independent of research, with no assigned intervention, arms, randomization, masking, placebo or investigational product. Index dates are 1 January–31 August 2025; records are confined to 2 December 2024–31 December 2025.

The primary endpoint is follow-up-minus-baseline logMAR with habitual distance correction in the fixed study eye. Baseline uses Days -30 through -1 and follow-up Days 28–70, targeting Day 42; negative change is better and positive worse. The secondary endpoint is the proportion with at least one study-eye pressure of 25 mmHg or higher on Days 1–7, among people with an observed pressure in that eye/window. Each person counts once. Selection, tie and missingness rules are specified in Informed Consent / Subject Enrollment. These historical windows are not research appointments.

Consecutive inclusion, deduplication, fixed-eye selection and predefined measurement/window rules limit discretionary choices; apply the detailed rules in Informed Consent / Subject Enrollment. Preserve recorded methods and treatment context, distinguish ambiguous/missing values from no elevation, and report endpoint-specific availability without imputation. Selection, measurement and attendance biases remain; change does not establish treatment efficacy.

This review has no prospective enrollment, participant signature process or recontact. Consent and privacy-authorization waivers will be requested; neither waiver nor IRB approval is granted. Obtain required ethics/privacy decisions and written site permission before research access.

Verify eligibility, deduplicate patient records and select one study eye per person: the earliest eligible routine laser procedure, with the right eye selected if both eligible eyes were treated on the same date. If no eligible eye remains, exclude the person. Keep this eye for all endpoints; missing measurements do not permit switching. Index procedures occur from 1 January through 31 August 2025, and accessible historical records from 2 December 2024 through 31 December 2025. Historical Day 0 is the selected eye's laser date, not enrollment.

Abstract age at procedure, sex, treated eye, index date, recorded ocular diagnoses, acuity with correction status/date/method, and pressure with date/method. Use distance acuity explicitly recorded in logMAR with habitual distance correction. Do not convert Snellen values, infer correction status or substitute near, uncorrected or fellow-eye acuity.

Baseline is the latest eligible value in Days -30 through -1, excluding procedure-day measurements. If several values occur on the latest date, use the last time-stamped eligible value; unresolved selection is ambiguous and missing. Follow-up is closest to Day 42 within Days 28–70. Equal-distance dates use the earlier date; multiple values on that date use the last time-stamped eligible value. Unresolved multiplicity remains ambiguous and missing. Do not widen windows or choose a favorable result. Missing measurements affect the applicable analysis, not cohort eligibility.

For early pressure elevation, use all recorded fixed-eye values in Days 1–7 and classify a person once if any is at least 25 mmHg. A person with no pressure measurement in that eye/window has missing status, not no elevation. Retain recorded method and treatment context without representing untreated pressure trajectories. There is no pressure-change endpoint.

Staff obtain decisions and permission, verify eligibility, deduplicate and identify eyes in November 2026; abstract in December–January; resolve permitted queries and lock coded data in February 2027; and analyze and report in March–April. Administrative closeout and archiving end on 31 May 2027. A record is complete after extraction and permitted queries are resolved, including missing/ambiguous codes. Study completion requires dataset lock, planned analyses and the aggregate report; archiving follows. These tasks do not extend the fixed clinical-record period.

If permission is withdrawn, suspend research access immediately. Resume only after documented authorization is restored. Otherwise stop further abstraction, preserve required records and report available data and limitations. No patient contact, replacement eye or new test may fill gaps.

No new acuity/pressure test, questionnaire, telephone call, clinic visit, imaging review, specimen or genetic activity occurs. There is no specimen transfer, storage, banking or future use. Site privacy requests follow applicable permissions without a prospective withdrawal visit or a promise to reverse already deidentified aggregate findings. Original clinical records remain at the clinic under its separate retention policy.

The overall cohort contains all eligible unique people, including those lacking outcome measurements. The primary analysis uses people with both selected habitual-correction logMAR values in the fixed eye; the secondary analysis uses people with a pressure record in that eye on Days 1–7. Report contributing people separately for each endpoint. Missing data affect only the relevant analysis, not cohort eligibility.

Calculate primary change as selected follow-up minus baseline logMAR. Report contributing people, mean change, standard deviation, a 95% confidence interval, median and range. Negative change is better recorded acuity; positive is worse.

For the secondary proportion, report the number with any recorded pressure at least 25 mmHg divided by people with at least one pressure measurement in the fixed eye on Days 1–7. Use all recorded values in the window but count each person once. No record means missing rather than no elevation. There is no secondary pressure-change endpoint.
Use available observations without imputation and report missing, ambiguous and unavailable measurement types separately with explicit denominators. There is no paired-eye or adjusted subgroup model.

Results are descriptive, without confirmatory significance claims or causal conclusions. Selection, measurement and attendance biases limit interpretation. No additional exploratory outcome is planned.
All eligible records; 150 people is a feasibility estimate, with no formal power calculation, assumed effect size or prospective attrition rate.

Authorized site research staff access identifiers only for eligibility and linkage on the clinic's encrypted access-controlled drive, storing the study-ID key separately. Analysts and sponsor receive study ID, age at index, relative-day intervals and coded clinical data without names, contacts, birth dates, exact clinical dates or keys. Exact dates remain in restricted source records. Authorized monitors, the reviewing IRB and legally authorized oversight bodies may inspect relevant originals under applicable permissions.

Publish aggregate results only, suppressing cells below five and complementary cells revealing suppressed counts. There is no individual public dataset, identifying case report, data sale or unrelated future research.

Keep research data, keys, permissions and abstraction logs securely for six years after 31 May 2027 closeout, then destroy research copies unless binding requirements require longer. Original clinical records follow the clinic's separate policy and are not destroyed by the study. Site privacy requests follow applicable permissions without a promise to reverse already deidentified aggregate findings.

The research risk is loss of confidentiality, mitigated by restricted access, separate keys and aggregate reporting. No new physical procedure or prospective adverse-event collection occurs. The PI handles suspected privacy incidents under site policy and required ethics/privacy reporting arrangements; no reporting-hour deadline is supplied.

Elmstead Independent Research Review Board, independent of sponsor and clinic, is the designated reviewing body. The study has not been submitted and no approval, approval number or date exists. Consent and privacy-authorization waivers will be requested, not presumed granted. Required decisions and site permission precede access. Permission withdrawal and resumption are handled as specified in Informed Consent / Subject Enrollment, without patient recontact.

There is no direct benefit, participant payment, reimbursement or new clinical charge. The sponsor funds staff work and analysis; no new injury-treatment or insurance promise is established. No child records are included.
